correctness.rationale: All-pairs shortest paths decompose through the shared articulation, so convex hypotheses containing the root factor into rooted convex families and root-avoiding nonempty hypotheses lie within one factor. Traces on multi-factor supports are exactly rooted-shatterable; singleton-factor and root-containing supports give the correction -(t-1)z. A complete gap characterization on each cycle yields the rooted quadratic and unrooted cubic polynomials, with an explicit finite-gap triple count and four-point obstruction. The degree argument proves the maximum support coefficient and VC dimension. Independent brute-force graph-distance code checks 1,089 ordered pairs of rooted graphs, cycles through order 12 and six mixed bouquets; these finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new contribution is the identity for the entire shattered-support enumerator under a one-vertex graph sum, plus the heterogeneous cycle-bouquet formula and maximum-support coefficient. Existing general graph-geodesic VC bounds, convex-geometric shattering systems, and halfspace VC results concern distinct or less enumerative assertions, and earlier one-cycle formulas do not imply the one-vertex gluing law without additional proof. Relevant statements from three freely accessible primary full texts were inspected and compared; searches found no dominating claim. An equivalent rooted convolution under other terminology remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: This is a coefficientwise structural decomposition theorem for all finite graphs joined at a cut vertex, rather than a scalar dimension bound. It yields an exact complete support polynomial, length-independent 2t VC dimension, and length-dependent number of maximum shattered supports for every bouquet of t>=2 cycles of arbitrary heterogeneous lengths. The formula permits compositional enumeration on block structures and captures phenomena not visible in isolated cycle data.
